name: Podiatry & Foot Surgery
tagline: Eliminate Routine Foot Care Denials & Modifier-25 Audits
summary: Podiatric billing is fraught with strict Medicare Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs), routine foot care statutory exclusions, and aggressive clawbacks on Modifier-25 and Q-modifiers. Provider Billers eliminates non-covered denials and accelerates surgical procedure reimbursements.
denialHotspots: CMS statutory exclusion denials for routine foot care (PR-204) without qualifying systemic metabolic disease documentation
Modifier-25 bundle rejections on same-day E/M visits alongside nail debridement or mycotic nail trimming
Missing or invalid class findings (Q7, Q8, Q9) and absence of attending MD NPI on diabetic nail care claims
Pre-authorization lapses on advanced wound care biologics and synthetic skin substitutes (Q4100 series)

keyCptCodes.description: Paring or cutting of benign hyperkeratotic lesion (eg, corn, callus); single lesion
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied as routine care unless backed by documentation of severe peripheral vascular disease or diabetes with qualifying class findings.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Automate verification of systemic qualifying conditions and attach mandatory Q7/Q8/Q9 modifiers with referring physician NPI.

keyCptCodes.description: Debridement of nails, any method(s); 6 or more
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Frequently downcoded or bundled with evaluation visits under Medicare LCDs when billed more often than once every 60 days.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Enforce strict 61-day date-of-service rules and ensure secondary ICD-10 diagnosis (e.g., onychomycosis L60.2 with pain) is documented.

keyCptCodes.description: Correction, hammertoe (eg, interphalangeal fusion, phalangectomy)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied for missing anatomical digit modifiers (T1-T9, TA) or bundled with bunionectomies without appropriate unbundling modifiers.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Append exact digit modifiers and verify bundling edits against NCCI mutually exclusive column pairs.

keyCptCodes.description: Office or other outpatient visit for established patient with separate procedure
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Automatic payer pre-payment audit or immediate denial when billed with same-day minor surgical procedures.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Ensure distinct documentation demonstrating a significant, separately identifiable medical decision (Modifier-25 compliant).

modifiers.rule: Mandatory when billing an E/M visit on the same day as nail debridement (11721) or lesion excision (11055); must document independent medical necessity.
Identifies specific class findings (absence of pulses, skin changes) required by Medicare contractors to reimburse routine foot care.
Used to bill separate anatomical anatomical sites (e.g. separate toe surgery during same operative session) to bypass NCCI edits.

recoveryStrategy: We audit your last 90 days of EOBs, identify all misapplied routine exclusions, re-attach compliant ICD-10 systemic indicators with attending MD dates of last visit, and appeal past write-offs to recapture lost clinic revenue.

faqs.q: How do you overturn Medicare denials for nail debridement (CPT 11721)?
faqs.a: Medicare requires specific systemic diseases (e.g., peripheral neuropathy, diabetes mellitus) accompanied by severe clinical indicators. We configure your billing scrubbers to verify the 60-day interval rule and require documented class findings before electronic submission.

faqs.q: Can we bill an office visit (99213/99214) with an in-office injection or wart excision?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the documentation clearly reflects an evaluation beyond the typical pre-procedure work. We train your staff on Modifier-25 clinical separation to withstand payer audits.

name: Cardiology & Interventional Care
tagline: Overcome Echo, Stress Test & Imaging Denials with Prior Auth Precision
summary: Cardiology billing demands flawless handling of professional vs. technical split billing (Modifiers 26/TC), strict medical necessity algorithms for diagnostic imaging, and rapid prior authorization turnaround for invasive catheterization and cardiac PET/SPECT.
denialHotspots: Diagnostic cardiac ultrasound (93306) denied for non-covered secondary ICD-10 indications or lack of documented symptoms
Failure to split professional and technical components (26 vs. TC) across hospital-affiliated vs. private lab settings
Nuclear SPECT/PET stress test denials due to missing peer-to-peer authorization or unverified tracer HCPCS codes (A9500)
Denied telemetry monitoring (93228/93229) exceeding standard duration limits without documented arrhythmia recurrence

keyCptCodes.description: Electrocardiogram, routine ECG with at least 12 leads; with interpretation and report
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied when billed during the same encounter as a cardiac consult or stress test without separate clinical rationale.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Audit whether the clinic owns the ECG machine (global 93000) or only performed interpretation (93010) in an outpatient facility.

keyCptCodes.description: Echocardiography, transthoracic, real-time with image documentation (2D), includes M-mode, spectral & color Doppler
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Payers frequently deny 93306 claiming routine surveillance is non-covered without documented murmurs, palpitations, or heart failure.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Implement clinical decision support scrubbers validating primary ICD-10 codes (I50.9, R01.1, I48.91) before claim dispatch.

keyCptCodes.description: Cardiovascular stress test using maximal or submaximal treadmill or bicycle; with continuous ECG and physician supervision
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Rejected when split across multiple entities without clear breakdown of supervision (-26) and facility tracer usage.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Accurately parse global vs. component billing based on location of service (POS 11 vs. POS 22).

keyCptCodes.description: Left heart catheterization including intraprocedural coronary angiography and left ventriculography
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied for missing prior authorization reference numbers or lack of documented hemodynamic measurement logs in operative notes.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Reconcile authorization numbers with hospital pre-registration and submit clean operative summaries on first pass.

modifiers.rule: Professional component only; used when physician interprets cardiac studies performed at an outside imaging center or hospital.
Technical component only; covers equipment, technicians, and supplies when billed by an independent diagnostic testing facility.
Distinguishes distinct diagnostic services from surgical catheterizations performed during the same operative intervention.

recoveryStrategy: Our team cross-references all cardiac imaging remits against payer-specific LCD guidelines, identifies missing 26/TC splits, and refiles zero-balance denials within 72 hours.

faqs.q: Why do commercial payers frequently reject our 93306 echo claims?
faqs.a: Commercial carriers like UnitedHealthcare and Aetna utilize AIM Specialty Health or eviCore medical necessity algorithms. If the pre-service clinical notes lack documented chest pain, syncope, or ejection fraction metrics, denials trigger automatically. We capture pre-service data beforehand.

faqs.q: How do you recover aged cardiology AR (>90 days)?
faqs.a: We assign senior RCM auditors to pull aged AR reports, run batch eligibility and timely filing appeals, and contact payer medical directors directly for retro-authorizations where allowed.

name: Mental & Behavioral Health
tagline: Master Time-Based Psychotherapy Billing & Session Unit Guardrails
summary: Psychiatry and behavioral health clinics struggle with strict time-based psychotherapy coding rules, session frequency caps, interactive complexity billing, and evolving telehealth parity laws across commercial payers and Medicaid.
denialHotspots: Psychotherapy claims denied for insufficient time documentation (e.g. failing to meet the CPT time midpoint rule)
Unbundled E/M med management (99213) with add-on psychotherapy (+90833) denied for lack of clinical separation
Telehealth place-of-service mismatch (POS 02 vs. POS 10) and missing audio-only or video modifiers (-95 / -FQ)
Exceeded annual session limits or missing outpatient treatment authorizations on commercial behavioral health carve-outs

keyCptCodes.description: Psychotherapy, 45 minutes with patient (38-52 minutes documentation required)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied or downcoded during payer audits if exact start and stop times or total session duration are omitted from progress notes.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Enforce strict EHR templates that capture exact session duration and progress toward treatment plan goals.

keyCptCodes.description: Psychotherapy, 60 minutes with patient (53+ minutes documentation required)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Heavily targeted by insurers (e.g., Optum, BCBS) with automated frequency audits and demand for clinical justification over 90834.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Document clinical justification for extended session length (e.g., trauma processing, acute crisis de-escalation) on every claim.

keyCptCodes.description: Psychotherapy, 30 minutes with patient, when performed with an evaluation and management service (List separately)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied when billed alone or without a primary established patient E/M code (e.g., 99213 or 99214).
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Ensure dual-note documentation: separate paragraph for psychiatric somatic/med evaluation and separate section for psychotherapy technique.

keyCptCodes.description: Interactive complexity (List separately in addition to code for primary service)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Rejected when billed without meeting one of the four specific statutory communication barrier criteria (e.g. caregiver discord, translator, third-party involvement).
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Include the specific statutory reason in note templates to ensure bulletproof reimbursement.

modifiers.rule: Synchronous telemedicine service rendered via real-time interactive audio and video telecommunications system.
Audio-only telehealth encounters; required by Medicare and certain commercial carriers when video technology is unavailable.
Provider specialty identifiers (Psychiatrist vs. Clinical Psychologist / Licensed Clinical Social Worker) required by state Medicaid programs.

recoveryStrategy: We systematically verify carve-out behavioral health administrators (e.g., Magellan, Beacon, Optum Behavioral), audit session time logs, and recover historical write-offs caused by administrative POS mismatches.

faqs.q: Why does Optum or Blue Cross frequently audit our 90837 claims?
faqs.a: Payers view 90837 as higher cost than 90834. They run automated outlier reports against regional peer averages. We safeguard your practice by validating medical necessity and ensuring start/stop timestamps are airtight.

faqs.q: How do you handle separate behavioral health carve-outs?
faqs.a: Many medical insurance cards outsource mental health benefits to third-party carve-outs. Our front-end eligibility team checks exact behavioral claims addresses before billing to stop 30-day dead-ends.

name: Orthopedic Surgery & Sports Medicine
tagline: Protect High-Value Surgical Claims & Master Global Period Billing
summary: Orthopedic surgery accounts for some of the highest-dollar claims in outpatient and inpatient medicine. Denials commonly stem from misunderstood 90-day global surgical packages, assistant surgeon modifiers, multiple procedure discounts, and unbundled DME supplies.
denialHotspots: Post-operative E/M visits denied within the 90-day global surgical period without Modifier-24 or Modifier-79
Assistant at surgery claims (CPT -80 / -82 / -AS) rejected due to payer-specific surgical policy restrictions
Multiple arthroscopic procedures improperly unbundled or subject to aggressive 50% second-procedure reductions
Fracture care (e.g., 27244, 27506) denials when casting/splinting supplies (Q4000 series) are billed without separate identifiers

keyCptCodes.description: Arthroscopy, knee, surgical; with meniscectomy (medial OR lateral, including any meniscal shaving)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Payers bundle debridement or synovectomy in the same compartment, denying secondary arthroscopy codes.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Enforce anatomical modifiers (e.g., lateral vs. medial compartment) and verify NCCI mutually exclusive column guidelines.

keyCptCodes.description: Arthroplasty, knee, condyle and plateau; medical and lateral compartments with or without patella resurfacing (total knee arthroplasty)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: High-cost implant hardware denied when separate invoice documentation or specific HCPCS codes (C1776) are missing.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Include detailed implant manufacturer logs and itemized cost reports in the initial submission packet.

keyCptCodes.description: Arthrocentesis, aspiration and/or injection, major joint or bursa (eg, shoulder, hip, knee, joint); without ultrasound guidance
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied when billed on the same day as an office visit without Modifier-25, or billed with ultrasound without code 20611.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Ensure injection notes specify anatomical joint, medication dosage (J-codes), and separate reason for encounter.

keyCptCodes.description: Arthroscopy, shoulder, surgical; with rotator cuff repair
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Billed alongside subacromial decompression (29826) without confirming whether payer requires an add-on code or distinct modifier.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Cross-check annual AMA CPT updates regarding shoulder arthroscopy bundling conventions.

modifiers.rule: Unrelated evaluation and management service by the same physician during a post-operative period (e.g., patient seen for knee pain during shoulder 90-day global).
Unrelated procedure or service by the same physician during the post-operative period (e.g., emergency fracture reduction on contralateral limb).
Assistant surgeon services: Modifier-80 for MD/DO assistants; Modifier-AS for Physician Assistants (PA) or Nurse Practitioners (NP).

recoveryStrategy: We perform granular operative note reviews to capture missed surgical components, appeal unbundled denials with operative reports highlighted by certified orthopedics coders, and recover trapped high-dollar surgical revenue.

faqs.q: How do you recover payment for visits during the 90-day global surgery period?
faqs.a: When an established patient returns during the 90-day window for a new issue or unrelated trauma, payers deny by default. We scrub records to ensure Modifier-24 is paired with a distinct diagnosis code and medical narrative.

faqs.q: Can you collect unpaid DME (braces, splints, walkers) for our clinic?
faqs.a: Yes. DME billing requires DMEPOS Medicare supplier numbers, proof of delivery certificates, and specific HCPCS codes. We eliminate DME write-offs through front-end documentation checklists.

name: Family Practice & Internal Medicine
tagline: Master Preventive vs. Problem-Oriented Splitting & Medicare AWVs
summary: Primary care clinics balance high patient volumes with razor-thin margins. The number one source of lost revenue is failure to properly bill same-day problem visits during preventive physicals, missed Chronic Care Management (CCM), and unbilled Medicare Annual Wellness Visits (AWV).
denialHotspots: Patient surprise bills and commercial denials when combining routine preventive physicals (99395/99396) with acute illness care (99214)
Medicare Annual Wellness Visits (G0438 / G0439) rejected due to incorrect eligibility timing (billed within 365 days of previous AWV)
Denial of in-office laboratory testing (CLIA-waived tests like 81002, 87880) for missing Modifier-QW
Uncaptured Chronic Care Management (99490) and Principal Care Management reimbursement due to time tracking gaps

keyCptCodes.description: Office or other outpatient visit for established patient, moderate medical decision making (30-39 minutes)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Downcoded to 99213 by commercial algorithmic scrubbers when documentation lacks moderate prescription drug management.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Align documentation with 2021/2023 AMA E/M guidelines emphasizing Medical Decision Making (MDM) complexity.

keyCptCodes.description: Annual wellness visit; includes a personalized prevention plan of service (PPS), initial (G0438) or subsequent (G0439)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied for frequency if submitted 1 day before the exact 12-month anniversary of the patient's prior wellness check.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Integrate real-time Medicare HETS/Noridian eligibility verification directly into the scheduling workflow.

keyCptCodes.description: Periodic comprehensive preventive medicine reevaluation and management, established patient; 40-64 years
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied by commercial insurers when combined with 99213/99214 without clinical evidence of two distinct services.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Split chart notes cleanly: Section 1 for age-appropriate screening, Section 2 with Modifier-25 addressing chronic condition exacerbations.

keyCptCodes.description: Chronic care management services with at least 20 minutes of clinical staff time per calendar month
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied for missing signed patient consent forms or unverified chronic disease qualifications (2 or more expected to last 12+ months).
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Establish care management logs tracking cumulative clinical staff minutes and automated monthly batch billing.

modifiers.rule: Crucial for primary care to capture revenue when a patient presenting for a physical also requires treatment for uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes.
Mandatory for CLIA-waived in-office laboratory tests (rapid strep, urinalysis, influenza, Covid-19 antigen) to prevent immediate claims rejection.
Identifies ACA preventive services billed without patient cost-sharing (co-pay / deductible).

recoveryStrategy: We audit 6 months of your E/M bell curve, identify under-coded 99213 visits that met 99214 criteria, recover rejected AWVs, and establish a recurring revenue pipeline for chronic care management.

faqs.q: Can our doctors legitimately bill both an annual physical (99395) and an office visit (99214) on the same day?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Under AMA guidelines and CMS rules, when a patient presents for a preventive exam and an acute or chronic condition requires significant additional medical decision-making, both are reimbursable with Modifier-25.

faqs.q: Why do our in-office rapid strep and urinalysis tests get rejected by Medicare?
faqs.a: CLIA-waived tests must include Modifier-QW and the clinic's CLIA certificate number in box 23 of the CMS-1500 form. We ensure every claim scrubber enforces this rule.

name: Neurology & Neuromuscular Medicine
tagline: Optimize EEG, EMG/NCS & Complex Chronic Neurological Care
summary: Neurology practices face complex billing challenges encompassing prolonged EEG monitoring, nerve conduction studies (NCS) combined with needle electromyography (EMG), and high-cost botulinum toxin injections for chronic migraine or spasticity.
denialHotspots: EMG/NCS claims denied when nerve conduction studies exceed payer clinical threshold limits without documented radiculopathy
Botox (J0585) injections denied for missing discarded waste documentation (Modifier -JW) or unverified FDA diagnostic indications
Routine video EEG monitoring (95700 series) rejected due to pre-authorization discrepancies with regional payers
Prolonged outpatient visit codes (+99417) denied for lack of continuous time tracking in E/M documentation

keyCptCodes.description: Nerve conduction studies; 7-8 studies
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Payers bundle studies or deny as medically unnecessary without precise limb-by-limb clinical rationale.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Enforce strict anatomical mapping and medical record attachment demonstrating neuromuscular diagnostic criteria.

keyCptCodes.description: Needle electromyography, each extremity, with related paraspinal areas; complete
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied when billed without an accompanying nerve conduction base code (95907-95913).
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Configure automated charge scrubbing linking add-on EMG codes directly to the qualifying NCS service.

keyCptCodes.description: Chemodenervation of muscle(s); facial and neck muscles for chronic migraine (Botox)
keyCptCodes.denialTrap: Denied if medical record fails to prove trial of at least 2 oral prophylactic migraine medications.
keyCptCodes.complianceFix: Verify prior authorization approvals and bill exact injection units alongside J0585 and JW modifier for wasted units.

modifiers.rule: Mandatory CMS reporting for single-dose vial drug waste (JW) or zero waste (JZ) on high-cost biologics like Botox.
Used for professional interpretation of hospital or remote continuous EEG monitoring.

recoveryStrategy: We audit high-volume electrodiagnostic claims against Medicare LCD frequency limits, recover unpaid biologic injections, and streamline prior authorizations for advanced migraine therapies.

faqs.q: How do we prevent Botox denials for chronic migraine?
faqs.a: Payers require precise documentation: 15+ headache days per month (at least 8 migraine days), documented failure of oral preventatives, and accurate J0585 unit calculation. We verify authorization before the vial is opened.
